name: Pro Tools
comment: Pro Tools key bindings, reproduced as an interface convention under ADR-0004, checked against Avid's Pro Tools Shortcuts Guide (12.5, 2021.6, 2025.6); see brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md. Modifiers are written in the Windows/Linux spelling: ctrl here is Command on a Mac keyboard, alt is Option. Numeric-keypad bindings assume Pro Tools' Transport keypad mode. Bindings marked "origin": "sonora" are ours, for commands Pro Tools has no key for; "verified": false marks a Pro Tools binding nobody has confirmed - see keymaps/README.md. Single keys marked "focus": "commands" are Commands Keyboard Focus bindings (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3, Commands Keyboard Focus Shortcuts): in the Qt window they run only while Commands Keyboard Focus is on, toggled by ctrl+alt+1 (Command+Option+1) or the a-z button. A terminal has no a-z indicator, so there they are always live, as before.

alt+return.comment: Option+Return on a Mac. On Windows Pro Tools uses Control+Enter instead; this profile follows the Mac set throughout.

numpad_3.comment: Avid's own guide disagrees with itself: the Transport keypad table calls keypad 3 Record Enable, the Recording table lists it under Start record. This follows the second.

alt+l.comment: Loop Record mode on/off, Option+L, a record mode apart from Loop Playback. Listed as Pro Tools' own in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md section 5, without a quotation from Avid's guide.

numpad_7.comment: Click on/off, 7 on the numeric keypad in Transport mode. Not yet checked against Avid's guide in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md.

numpad_8.comment: Count Off on/off, 8 on the numeric keypad in Transport mode. Not yet checked against Avid's guide in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md.

ctrl+7.comment: Command+7 / Control+7. Pro Tools also engages the Smart Tool by holding F6+F7 or F7+F8 together; this schema binds one chord to one command and cannot express two keys held at once.

ctrl+alt+bracketright.comment: Avid prints Command+Option+[ or ] for vertical zoom without saying which is in; ] for in follows the horizontal pair.

e.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3). The focus-free form, Mac Control+E / Windows Start+E, needs a modifier this schema cannot spell.

ctrl+shift+s.comment: File > Save As, Shift+Command+S (Shift+Control+S on Windows). Not yet quoted from Avid's guide in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md. Save Copy In has no Pro Tools key and none here.

ctrl+equal.comment: Command+= / Control+=, Toggle Mix/Edit windows. Not yet checked against Avid's guide in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md.

ctrl+numpad_1.comment: Window > Transport, Command+1 on the numeric keypad (Ctrl+1 on Windows). Not yet checked against Avid's guide in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md.

numpad_enter.comment: New Memory Location, Enter on the numeric keypad. Not yet checked against Avid's guide in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md.

ctrl+numpad_5.comment: Window > Memory Locations, Command+5 on the numeric keypad (Ctrl+5 on Windows). Not yet checked against Avid's guide in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md.

ctrl+q.comment: Not listed in Avid's Shortcuts Guide; macOS convention.

a.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3).

s.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3).

d.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3).

f.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3).

g.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3).

b.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3).

p.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3). Avid's command moves the edit insertion to the previous track, which is the nearest thing the catalog has.

semicolon.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3). Avid's command moves the edit insertion to the next track.

ctrl+alt+1.comment: Command+Option+1 (Mac) / Control+Alt+1 (Windows): enable Commands Keyboard Focus for the Edit window (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3). Avid describes enabling it; that the same chord turns it off again, like the a-z button, is our reading.

alt+shift+7.comment: Edit > Trim Clip > Start to Insertion, Option+Shift+7: the focus-free form of A (brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md section 1.7).

alt+shift+8.comment: Edit > Trim Clip > End to Insertion, Option+Shift+8: the focus-free form of S (same note).

z.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus: Undo (Avid, Shortcuts Guide ch. 3; the research note's focus layout, PT-C and PT-B tables).

r.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus: Zoom Out Horizontally (same table).

t.comment: Commands Keyboard Focus: Zoom In Horizontally (same table).

comma.comment: Ch. 7, Editing, Nudging, and Trimming: Nudge back, Minus on the keypad or Comma in Commands Keyboard Focus. The research note's summary of the ch. 3 table calls comma a nudge-and-play key instead; unresolved until someone reads the table again.

period.comment: Ch. 7: Nudge forward, Plus on the keypad or Period in Commands Keyboard Focus. Same disagreement as comma.

shift+r.comment: Record enable the tracks holding the edit cursor or selection. This build has no selection yet, so until it does this key reports that it failed; the numbered arms below work today.

shift+1.comment: Ours, so an engineer at a tty can arm a numbered track without a selection. No bare Shift+1 appears in Avid's guides.

shift+2.comment: Ours, and it collides: in Pro Tools Shift+2 bypasses inserts A-E on the selected tracks.

shift+3.comment: Ours, and it collides: in Pro Tools Shift+3 bypasses inserts F-J on the selected tracks.

shift+4.comment: Ours, and it collides: in Pro Tools Shift+4 mutes sends A-E on the selected tracks.

shift+5.comment: Ours, and it collides: in Pro Tools Shift+5 mutes sends F-J on the selected tracks.

alt+shift+r.comment: Ours. Pro Tools arms every track by Option-clicking a record-enable button. Option+Shift+R appears in none of Avid's three guides.

alt+shift+w.comment: Ours. Moved off alt+shift+d, which is Pro Tools' Duplicate Tracks. Option+Shift+W appears in none of Avid's 12.5, 2021.6 or 2025.6 guides.

alt+shift+d.comment: Duplicate Tracks, Option+Shift+D: Shortcuts Guide ch. 8, Track Menu (brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md). The dialog's default choices, without the dialog: the active playlist, the inserts and the mix (ADR-0023).

ctrl+shift+n.comment: Track > New, Command+Shift+N: opens New Tracks, which asks how many. Not yet checked against Avid's guides in brain/research/protools-logic-key-bindings.md.
